en: Paper-doll model for Yale 11873654 (Zelda Fitzgerald paper dolls)

Everything the paper-doll demo needs, in one page, expressed as annotations on Yale's own canvases. The pieces, their pixel sizes and their image services all stay under collections.library.yale.edu; this page adds only what a source record cannot know, namely which of the fourteen cut pieces is a figure and which is a garment, where each piece sits on the derived uncut sheet, and where a figure's torso is so that a garment can be registered against it. Every number the demo draws is derived from these annotations at load time, and no image is re-hosted.
Yale source IIIF Manifest (Presentation API 3)
Yale University Library catalog record 11873654
Derived sheet: coordinate space, scale and behaviour

body.value: Yale's copy of this object is already cut out: the published manifest has one canvas per physical piece, fourteen recto/verso pairs, and no sheet canvas at all. The cutout use case still asks for a view of the uncut sheet, so the sheet here is derived rather than quoted. It is a virtual rectangle 17090 by 11030 units, where one unit is one pixel of Yale's scans, and every piece is given a home position on it. Home positions and footprints are normalised to that rectangle, so 0,0 is its top-left corner and 1,1 its bottom-right corner.

Scale assumption: all fourteen recto exposures are 3421-3468 px wide by 5609 px tall, which is one fixed camera setup photographing pieces the catalogue measures at 28-31 cm. The pixel-to-millimetre ratio is therefore common to every piece, so an outfit can be laid on a figure at a 1:1 ratio with no resizing and no per-piece scale hint. If a future instance mixes plates photographed at different magnifications, add a `scale` field to each piece body and multiply its footprint by it.

Transparency: the pieces are photographed on a near-black board, not a white one, so the demo recovers alpha in the browser by flooding inward from the crop border through pixels within a tolerance of that border's median colour. The tolerance below was chosen by comparing the resulting silhouette against an independent luminance-threshold segmentation of the same crops: mean intersection over union 0.989 across all fourteen pieces.

en: Condition of this copy: already cut, several figures partly dressed

body.value: The catalogue gives an extent of 8 paper dolls (5 male, 3 female) and 6 paper outfits (4 men's, 2 women's), and says that two of the outfits are taped onto figures in this copy. The fourteen recto canvases are exactly that count, so each canvas carries one piece and none carries a sheet of pieces. Several figures are also painted wearing something, which is why the demo treats a garment as an overlay on top of whatever the figure already shows rather than as a replacement for a bare body. Several dolls have lost arms, hands or feet, so the silhouette the flood fill recovers is the surviving paper, not the intended figure. Which two outfits are the taped ones cannot be told from the scans alone and is not asserted here.
